memory_update.text: PAR is the cleanest underfollowed public restaurant-tech candidate for this node because its POS, Punchh loyalty, PAR Ordering, payments, and back-office products directly map to first-party ordering and customer-data infrastructure.

NCR Voyix should remain in the Layer 1 universe as a messy-label restaurant POS and commerce infrastructure name, especially after divesting Digital Banking and reporting Retail/Restaurants as the core segments.

The restaurant customer-access chokepoint has two sides: aggregators such as DoorDash monetize demand access, while POS/ordering/loyalty vendors such as Toast, PAR, and NCR Voyix help brands preserve direct relationships and operating data.

Olo was a highly relevant public pure-play for online ordering, delivery integration, payments, and guest data, but Thoma Bravo completed its acquisition in September 2025; remove OLO from active US-listed candidate screens and use it only as private-market comp evidence.
Toast is the scaled reference leader for restaurant POS, payments, online ordering, branded app, marketing and loyalty; keep as benchmark, not primary underfollowed alpha lane.
PAR Technology is a high-relevance underfollowed candidate because Punchh loyalty, PAR POS, PAR Ordering and payments map directly to restaurant customer-data and direct-ordering infrastructure.
NCR Voyix is a messy post-spin underfollowed candidate; its Restaurants segment, POS software, kiosks, services and commerce platform may be a hidden restaurant digitization infrastructure asset.

Lightspeed Commerce is a lower-mid-cap US-listed restaurant POS/payments/online-ordering candidate, but restaurant-specific mix and profitability need verification because the platform also serves retail and other verticals.

Olo would normally be core to this node, but current public-listing status is unclear due to 2025 merger/change-of-control evidence; verify SEC delisting/merger completion before adding or excluding permanently.

The key bottleneck metrics for later layers are restaurant location count, ARR, net revenue retention, payment attach rate, loyalty/digital ordering attach rate, customer concentration, integration breadth, and disclosed impact on third-party marketplace commission leakage.
PAR is the highest-priority underfollowed public candidate for restaurant first-party ordering, loyalty, POS, and customer-data infrastructure because its disclosed products map directly to the node.
NCR Voyix is a lower-attention restaurant POS and commerce infrastructure candidate, but the thesis depends on post-divestiture restaurant segment execution and recurring software growth.

Olo would have been the cleanest public pure-play for restaurant ordering, payments, and guest engagement, but it is no longer US-listed after Thoma Bravo completed its acquisition and delisting in September 2025.

For this node, the bottleneck is less physical supply and more control of customer access: POS, loyalty, order-routing, delivery integration, and payments vendors can become embedded infrastructure if restaurants prioritize first-party data and lower marketplace commission leakage.

PAR is a priority underfollowed candidate for restaurant loyalty, ordering, POS, payments, and customer-data infrastructure; verify subscription metrics, customer wins, retention, and enterprise chain exposure.
NCR Voyix is a messy but direct restaurant commerce infrastructure candidate; verify restaurant segment economics after spin/sale simplification and avoid over-crediting retail exposure.

SoundHound AI belongs in the speculative shadow lane for restaurant voice ordering and drive-thru automation; require restaurant-specific revenue, deployment, and integration evidence before upgrading.

Olo was one of the cleanest public restaurant ordering and guest-engagement software comps but is no longer US-listed after the 2025 Thoma Bravo acquisition; use it as a private-market comp, not a candidate.

summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Layer 1B expansion for the restaurant customer-access/data node found two reference anchors and two underfollowed public infrastructure names. DoorDash is the obvious marketplace-access reference because it taxes restaurant demand through delivery and merchant services. Toast is a large, direct restaurant operating-system leader but no longer underfollowed. The more Serenity-relevant discovery candidates are PAR Technology and NCR Voyix: both sit inside restaurant POS, loyalty, ordering, payments, and operational data workflows where restaurants try to defend direct customer relationships and reduce channel leakage. Olo was highly relevant historically but appears no longer US-listed after Thoma Bravo completed its acquisition in September 2025, so it is treated as a coverage gap rather than a candidate. Layer 1B expands the public-company universe around restaurant customer-access infrastructure. The reference lane is Toast, which is the clearest scaled restaurant operating-system anchor. The underfollowed lane is more interesting for this node: PAR Technology, NCR Voyix, and Lightspeed Commerce all sit in POS, payments, ordering, loyalty, kitchen/display, and restaurant workflow layers that help restaurants preserve first-party orders, guest data, and margin versus delivery marketplaces. Olo would normally be a core candidate, but current search evidence indicates a 2025 merger/change-of-control trail, so it is excluded pending confirmation of current public listing status.
